rules.statement: Run work that happens after a database commit, such as recording an audit event, on its own bounded post-commit cancellation token rather than the request's token, and do it inside the shared recorder so no call site can drop the record.
rules.why: If the client disconnects after the commit, the change stays committed but a request-token-bound lookup or publish can be cancelled, dropping the audit record and breaking the promise to audit every change.
rules.check: Look for audit or event recording calls after `SaveChangesAsync` that pass the request `CancellationToken` (or `HttpContext.RequestAborted`), including preliminary lookups the recorder does before it publishes.

rules.statement: In test code, apply the hoisting rule too: assign a call's result to a local before passing it to an assertion, rather than nesting the call inside `Assert.*` arguments.
rules.why: The house rule against nesting calls inside other calls' arguments applies to tests as well as production code, for readability and debuggability.
rules.check: Look for assertions such as `Assert.Equal(x, GetSomething(...).Count)` or `Assert.Single(GetSomething(...), ...)` with a method call inside the arguments.

rules.statement: Don't ask to bundle a shared template method's parameters into a parameter type when each parameter is a distinct concept and the type would only exist to carry them for that one call.
rules.why: Such a type moves the argument list into an initializer without removing a concept, and callers stay short calls anyway.
rules.check: Before flagging a method with four data parameters, check whether the parameters are distinct concepts (request, target, configuration, callback) and whether a grouping type would be used anywhere else.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask test classes to move their own mock-setup helpers into a shared test support type just because similar small helpers appear in several classes: each test class owns the strict-mock setups for its own subject.
rules.why: A test reads its arrangement in its own file and each class verifies its own mocks; sharing a few-line helper would couple the test classes through a support type.
rules.check: Before reporting duplicated setup helpers across test classes, check whether each helper configures that class's own mock fields and whether sibling test classes follow the same per-class setup pattern.

rules.statement: In a test project, group tests in `#region` blocks named for the member or operation under test (such as `AddTeamAdmin Tests`), including in feature-oriented integration test files.
rules.why: The test layout convention applies to integration suites too, matching sibling suites.
rules.check: Look for test methods placed directly in the class outside any `<Member> Tests` region, with only a `Scaffolding` region or none.

rules.statement: Don't flag a discouraged name suffix such as `*Manager` when the new type follows a naming pattern already established by its sibling components for the same role.
rules.why: Following the existing pattern lets a reader find every such component by one name pattern.
rules.check: Before reporting a naming-rule departure, check whether sibling types or components with the same responsibility already use the same suffix.
